headline: Best Buy's domestic comps jump 4.5% on computing and AI glasses; full-year sales and EPS outlook raised sharply.
guidance_note: FY27 revenue raised to $42.3-42.8B (from $41.2-42.1B), comps 1.9-3.0% (from -1% to +1%), adj EPS $6.70-6.90 (from $6.30-6.60); Q3 comp guide +1-3%.
key_messages: Domestic comp +4.5% (vs +1.1% a year ago); enterprise comp +4.1%, the strongest in years, beating expectations.
Computing was the biggest driver, its 10th straight quarter of positive comps; home theater, AI glasses and trading cards also grew.
Memory-cost inflation pushed computing ASPs up mid-teens while units fell high single digits; traditional gaming declined.
Gross margin rose ~70bps to 23.9%, helped by Marketplace, Best Buy Ads and ~$34M of IEEPA tariff refunds.
August comps tracking near the top of the Q3 guide; Barry's last call before Jason Bonfig becomes CEO on Nov. 1.

consumer.big_ticket: Customers still buy higher-priced tech when replacing devices or when innovation is compelling; computing replacement cycle continues, gaming down.
consumer.pricing: Memory component costs are raising computing prices (ASP up mid-teens, units down); one-time IEEPA tariff refunds aided margin.
consumer.quote: We are very pleased to report we outperformed expectations in the second quarter with comparable sales growth of 4.1% and a higher-than-expected adjusted operating income rate.

macro_read: Tech spending is recovering on replacement needs and new gadgets, but higher memory costs mean consumers buy fewer, pricier PCs; the shopper is selective, not retrenching.

sources.label: Best Buy corporate news: Q2 FY27
Barchart: Best Buy Reports Second Quarter Results

notes: About $34M of IEEPA tariff refunds helped gross margin; the per-share effect was not disclosed and is likely small.
